clue.text: Less is written about one British form of transport

indicators.note: a word written around other letters encloses them, so these letters go round the next pieces

parts.note: less, as in subtraction, is minus
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A grammar point: the word 'less' written about some British mode of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bus for a handful of passengers is a kind of road vehicle people travel in.

clue.text: Agree to change after millions becomes inadequate

indicators.note: the jumbled word comes after the abbreviation in the answer
to change the word agree means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Agreeing to alter a deal worth millions turns out to be poor value.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or insufficient in amount.

clue.text: Review advice that's given at work?

definitions.meaning: a newspaper write-up of a play or book
formal warning of dismissal or resignation handed over in the workplace

explanation.surface: A performance appraisal handed out by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic's write-up is one sense; formal warning to leave a job, given by employer or employee, is the other.

clue.text: Support teams accepting student reverts to type

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the student letter goes inside

parts.note: sides are teams
L is a learner driver's plate, hence a student

explanation.surface: Fans of sports teams let in a student who returns to old habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'student' is L from the learner plate British drivers display; 'accepting' tucks it into the teams word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who backslides relapses into former bad habits, falling back on their old nature.

clue.text: Second unlikely delay

parts.note: a tall story is an unlikely one

explanation.surface: A further, improbable hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: TALL as 'unlikely' comes from the phrase tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time or hold things up.

clue.text: Fish people oddly want?

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions of the word people

parts.note: to want something is to lack it

explanation.surface: A fishmonger asks whether the public really want it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'people', giving POL.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollack is a food fish of the cod family found in North Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Book written to make money on grass heating unit

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: pot and grass are both slang for cannabis
a boiler is a central heating unit

explanation.surface: A cash-in novel about cannabis and central heating.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a hastily written work produced just to earn a living.

clue.text: Slump, seeing money is short

indicators.note: short means the money word loses its final letter

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone slumps when cash is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: LOLLY is British slang for cash; 'is short' trims it to LOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to sit or lie in a lazy, sprawling way.

clue.text: Drink provided after a serving of tripe

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the rearranged letters
a serving is a dish made up from ingredients, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
provided means on condition that, or if

explanation.surface: A drink is taken once a plate of offal has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving of' turns A TRIPE into APERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An apéritif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to sharpen the appetite.

clue.text: Everything depends on this pitch's quality

parts.note: a musical key fixes pitch, so pitch is key, with the possessive kept
tone is the quality of a sound

explanation.surface: Everything hangs on the tone of a sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sales pitch or sports field, but here it is musical pitch; the definition is the whole opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The central stone of an arch holds the rest in place, so it is the thing all else relies upon.

clue.text: Room that's a credit, mostly — about time

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first letters surround the time abbreviation
mostly means the last letter of the word for credit is dropped

parts.note: on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: An estate agent praises a room as a credit to the house, more or less on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: On tick is British slang for on credit; 'about' wraps the A and the shortened credit word round the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A space just below the roof of a house is a loft, one room of the home.

clue.text: Trouble aboard vessel for part of the army

indicators.note: aboard means carried within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel
ill as a noun means trouble or harm

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out on a ship carrying troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks nautical but means a blood vessel here.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunners and their big guns form a branch of the land forces.

clue.text: Nut mostly found on reels for fish

indicators.note: found on means coming after the other piece in the answer

parts.note: to reel is to stagger or rock

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the nut

parts.note: an almond is a nut

explanation.surface: A nut, nearly whole, discovered on fishing reels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reels' looks like fishing tackle but is a verb meaning staggers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salmon is a fishmonger's trade name for dogfish and similar species sold as food.

clue.text: Handle line during strike

indicators.note: during means inside the span of, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: A handle gets a line drawn on it during industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a walkout but means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The grip of a sword or dagger is its handle.

clue.text: Occupation of goalie after match?

indicators.note: the goalie word comes after the match word in the answer

parts.note: a match is a game
a goalkeeper is a keeper

explanation.surface: What a goalkeeper does once the match is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to look after game birds on an estate holds a recognised job.

clue.text: An idiot getting upset about quiet process of producing alcohol

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the next piece
upset means knocked over and jumbled, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: still means quiet

explanation.surface: A fool gets upset about the quiet way spirits are made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AN IDIOT into DIATION, which 'about' wraps round STILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are made by boiling a fermented liquid and condensing the vapour, the standard method for strong drink.

clue.text: Follows a gang, lost in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means in a muddle, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone trails after a gang that has lost its way.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is to follow someone, often uninvited.

clue.text: Asked to go naked, revealed frame

indicators.note: going naked means stripping off the outer layer, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: to let on is to reveal

explanation.surface: Someone asked to strip reveals their figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go naked' strips A and D from ASKED, leaving SKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The bones form the body's supporting framework.

clue.text: Order coach

definitions.meaning: to direct someone to do something

explanation.surface: A bare pair of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to command and to teach.

clue.text: School rent gear out by type

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces stand next to each other

parts.note: kind means type or sort

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A school is renting out equipment of a certain kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A kindergarten is a nursery school for very young children.

clue.text: Break after a day at sea

indicators.note: the break word comes after the first two pieces

parts.note: a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A crew's holiday after a day of sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' reads as setting but is the definition: lost or confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting without mooring or direction, literally or figuratively lost.

clue.text: Nightmare of poor grades in exam

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
D and E are low marks

explanation.surface: Bad marks in a test are a student's nightmare.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrowing trial or terrible experience is a nightmare.

clue.text: Many schemes must ignore parking

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: plots are schemes
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Plenty of town plans have to leave out car parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots is an informal quantity word for a great number.

clue.text: Device that scans a person afraid of motor vehicles?

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle
someone who dreads something is a dreader of it

explanation.surface: A machine that reads cards, cast as someone frightened of cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'vehicles' is loose: one car stands for the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that reads the chip or stripe on a bank card or key card is a scanning device.

clue.text: Dean regularly absorbed by obscure material

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the next piece

parts.note: dim means obscure or faint

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of Dean

explanation.surface: A college dean is engrossed in some dark fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes E and N from Dean.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric, as used for jeans.

clue.text: Bond's rumoured nationality?

indicators.note: rumoured means spoken of, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tie is a bond or link

explanation.surface: Gossip about which country James Bond comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' points to 007 but means a tie, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand holds that nationality.

clue.text: Time that hurt depressed land

parts.note: ouch is what you say when something hurts
down means depressed or low

explanation.surface: A painful time leaves someone feeling low in a hard landing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft touching down is landing on the runway.

clue.text: Prepare for the best

definitions.meaning: to prepare a pump, a gun or a person is to make it ready

explanation.surface: Get ready for the finest outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means make ready; as a noun it means the peak or choicest part.

clue.text: Making a profit from open-weave material

definitions.meaning: to net money is to clear it as profit

explanation.surface: Someone earns money from selling loose-woven fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing a sum as profit is to net it; mesh fabric is also called net.

clue.text: Ruin one short story of marriage

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the story word is cut off

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A short story about how a marriage was wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital is the adjective for matters relating to wedlock and spouses.
